After a Villain's Arrest.text: After a villain is arrested, the case moves through the ordinary justice system with extra care for the Quirk. The suspect is taken to a police station in restraints suited to their Quirk and held in a holding cell rated for it: fireproof, sealed, padded or watched by camera as the power requires. Police may hold a suspect for questioning for a short period before prosecutors must ask a judge for detention, which can extend for weeks while the case is built. A Quirk assessment by a specialist records what the power can do. Dangerous suspects wait in Quirk-secure detention centers rather than local cells. Courts try villains under criminal law, and illegal Quirk use is added to the charges. Convicts serve sentences in prisons with wings built around common Quirk types; inmates whose Quirks no ordinary prison can hold go to specialized facilities, and the worst go to Tartarus. Released villains remain on the registry with a criminal record that follows them.
